description:
## Why

PKIX-ng0x decomposition, child 2 of 5. Once an AC is parsed, the next
layer is identifying which public-key cert holder the AC refers to.
RFC 5755 §4.2.2 defines three Holder identification mechanisms, each
needing its own binding logic.

## What

1. Public API on `AttributeCertificate`:
   - `fn holder_kind(&self) -> HolderKind` returning one of
     `BaseCertificateId`, `EntityName`, `ObjectDigestInfo`.
   - `fn binds_to(&self, pkc: &x509_cert::Certificate) -> Result<(), AcError>`
     that returns Ok when the AC binds to the supplied PKC.
2. Binding logic per Holder shape:
   - **baseCertificateID**: AC.holder.baseCertificateID.{issuer, serial}
     must equal the PKC.tbsCertificate.{issuer, serialNumber}. Issuer
     comparison must follow RFC 4518 DN comparison (already a project
     constraint) so cannot be byte-equal.
   - **entityName**: AC.holder.entityName.GeneralNames must contain a
     name that matches a GeneralName in the PKC subjectAltName or the
     PKC subject DN. Document the exact match semantics chosen and back
     them with RFC 5755 §4.2.2 paragraph references.
   - **objectDigestInfo**: hash the PKC public-key, full PKC, or other
     "object" per the AC.holder.objectDigestInfo.digestedObjectType
     and compare to the stored digest.
3. Errors: distinct `AcError` variants per binding failure mode so
   callers can distinguish "wrong serial" vs "name mismatch".

## Tests

- [ ] One fixture per Holder shape, with two test cases each:
      matching PKC succeeds, mismatched PKC fails with the right
      error variant.
- [ ] Independent oracle for objectDigestInfo: hash computed via
      openssl `dgst -sha256` against the input PKC pubkey DER,
      compared byte-equal.
- [ ] DN comparison must use the project canonical helper (not naive
      byte-equality).

## Depends on

PKIX-ng0x.1 (AC ASN.1 parser must exist first).

## Acceptance

- [ ] Three binding variants tested.
- [ ] DN comparison goes through the RFC 4518 helper.
- [ ] objectDigestInfo digest matches openssl-computed oracle.
title: pkix-ac: RFC 5755 §4.2.2 Holder identification + binding check
